maria_gonzalez: Kicking off a focused replay run to validate cohort-weighted sampling + KV-cache parity. Goal: apples-to-apples kernel selection and batching comparison vs prod traces while preserving anonymized cohort weights. I want to catch any nondeterminism that impacts latency or token counts.
jonathan_lee: 👍 what's the exact sampling plan? random sample or weighted by active sessions? we need to keep distribution of short vs long seqs.
devin_hsu: Plan: cohort-weighted sampling using user-id hash buckets -> sample proportional to traffic weight per cohort. Preserves short/long ratio. Using seed=42 to make runs reproducible. Also will include a control uniform sample for baseline.
sarah.k: Quick note on anonymization: we strip PII then replace user-id with stable cohort-id generated from a salted hash (salt stored in secret manager). That keeps cohort weighting consistent without exposing ids.
maria_gonzalez: Good. Two critical parity checks I want: 1) kernel selection parity: same kernel chosen given same model config + seq len distribution, 2) KV-cache warmup parity: replay must reconstruct KV state in same order so we can compare prefix cache hit ratios.
devin_hsu: Found a small nondeterminism earlier: kernel tie-breaker used runtime clock in some builds. I patched it to use deterministic preference order in kernel_selector::choose(). Will include the diff in the run artifacts.
jonathan_lee: can you paste the invocation you're running? want to replicate locally.
devin_hsu: Command:
```
./replay_harness --trace-dir s3://redwood-prod-traces/2026-02 --out run-2145009876 --sample-method cohort_weighted --seed 42 --anon-salt $SALT --kvcache-replay true --record-kernel-choices
```
perfbot: automated: replay_harness run queued (id=run-2145009876). Estimated time ~ 45m.
maria_gonzalez: We'll enable high-res profiling (perf counters + fine-grained tracer) for the first 5% of traffic, then normal sampling. This keeps overhead bounded.
sarah.k: On KV warmup: we should preserve original interleaving of user sessions to reproduce cache TTL effects. If we reorder by session start time vs arrival, hit ratios diverge.
devin_hsu: Implementation detail: harness preserves original arrival timestamps and injects them into the serving runtime via --replay-timestamp. That should keep batching behavior similar to prod. However batching heuristics also use a small jitter feature flag; set to production value to be apples-to-apples.
jonathan_lee: remind me which flags: `batching.jitter_ms` and `batching.max_batch_tokens` right?
devin_hsu: yes, plus `kernel_selector.prefer_fused_attention` (this was the one that caused a subtle change when seq_len < 64). Set those to prod-config.json for the run.
maria_gonzalez: Early result from partial run (first 10k requests): kernel selection parity = 99.2% (meaning 0.8% different). KV-cache prefix hits differ by +1.1% in replay vs prod (bad direction). Profiling shows most divergence in small-Seq (<64) buckets.
sarah.k: interesting — did we get a trace of one of the mismatches? devin, can you dump the raw decisions for a few mismatches.
devin_hsu: Pasted a sample mismatch (anonymized):
```
request_id: anon-c123
seq_len: 48
prod_kernel: attention_fused_f16
replay_kernel: attention_sparse_f16
batch_tokens_at_choice: 384
kernel_selector_log: "tie-break fallback to sparse when fused busy"
```
That fallback is due to a runtime occupancy signal that wasn't deterministic in our harness. I'm going to make occupancy inputs deterministic by replaying GPU queue depth snapshots.
jonathan_lee: That occupancy fallback explains latency delta for those requests. If occupancy is non-deterministic we can't expect perfect parity.
maria_gonzalez: Agreed. Action items: (1) make occupancy input deterministic, (2) rerun with kvcache warmup logging enabled (dump prefix cache keys for first N sessions), (3) compare histograms by bucket (seq_len and tokens/batch).
perfbot: automated: partial-run-summary for run-2145009876 (10k samples):
- avg latency diff (replay vs prod): +4.7ms
- p95 latency diff: +18ms
- kernel parity: 99.2%
- kvcache_prefix_hit_rate: prod=0.72 replay=0.731
- seed: 42

perfbot: artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/runs/run-2145009876/summary.json
sarah.k: The kvcache hit increase in replay might be due to preserved arrival but different interleaving of concurrent sessions (we're not modeling network backpressure). We'll need to simulate network concurrency constraints (max inflight per user) to match prod.
devin_hsu: I added a new flag `--simulate-inflight N` to cap concurrent requests per cohort; trying with 8 per cohort now.
maria_gonzalez: Great. Also add a regression check: if kernel parity < 99.5% or avg latency diff > 3ms, fail the run and open a ticket.
jonathan_lee: I'll make a quick script to compute parity by (model, seq_len_bucket, kernel_choice) and produce a delta heatmap. Will push to repo.
maria_gonzalez: Thanks. Let's reconvene when the deterministic occupancy + inflight limit run completes. If parity still fails in <64 bins, we should instrument the kernel_selector decision path more (add a debug-only deterministic log). 
devin_hsu: will do. tagging @sarah.k and @jonathan_lee for followups. :mag:
sarah.k: thanks. filing a short doc with sampling config and anonymization steps so PMs can reproduce. :memo:
maria_gonzalez: perfect. next checkpoint in ~2 hours after the rerun. :rocket:
